question: Hermey the elf hates making toys. What does he want to be instead?
hint: His dream job involves checkups and fillings.
funFact: Hermey was voiced by Paul Soles, who went on to voice Peter Parker in the 1967 Spider-Man cartoon.

question: What's the name of the bushy-bearded prospector who's always searching for silver and gold?
hint: His first name is a territory in northern Canada.
funFact: At the end, he licks his pickaxe and strikes it rich at last: “I've got me a peppermint mine!”

question: What does Rudolph's dad make him wear to hide his glowing red nose?
hint: It pops off at the Reindeer Games.
funFact: Before that, his dad tried covering it with mud.

question: What's the name of the friendly snowman who narrates the special and sings “A Holly Jolly Christmas”?
hint: He introduces himself with a three-letter first name.
funFact: He's voiced by folk singer Burl Ives, who was hired to please NBC and its sponsor, General Electric.

question: Where do Rudolph and Hermey meet a spotted elephant and a bird that swims instead of flies?
hint: Every toy there was unwanted.
funFact: The doll's flaw is never explained. Producer Arthur Rankin Jr. later said she'd been cast off by her owner and was clinically depressed.

question: Which young doe tells Rudolph he's cute, making him so happy he soars into the air?
hint: Her name rhymes with “police.”
funFact: Later she sings Rudolph the gentle ballad “There's Always Tomorrow.”

question: Who said it? “Whoever heard of a skinny Santa?”
hint: She's always fussing over Santa's dinner plate.
funFact: The often-quoted combo, “Eat, Papa, eat. Nobody likes a skinny Santa,” is a misquote: that exact line is never said.

question: Why does Charlie-in-the-Box think no child will ever want him?
answer: His name is Charlie instead of Jack
hint: Think about what that kind of toy is normally called.
funFact: He proudly calls himself the island's “official sentry.”

question: What does the misfit water pistol shoot?
hint: Something you'd spread on toast.
funFact: Its neighbors include a choo-choo train with square wheels, a cowboy who rides an ostrich and a boat that can't stay afloat.

question: How does Hermey make the Abominable Snow Monster harmless?
answer: He pulls out all its teeth
hint: Think about the elf's dream job.
funFact: Once he's reformed, the Bumble earns a job at Santa's place by putting the star on top of the Christmas tree, no stepladder needed.

question: Which of Santa's reindeer is Rudolph's father?
hint: His name is German for “thunder.”
funFact: Rudolph himself was voiced by a woman, Billie Mae Richards, who was credited as “Billy Richards.”

question: Rudolph's prospector pal survives going over a cliff with the Abominable Snow Monster. Finish his explanation: “Didn't I ever tell you about Bumbles? Bumbles…”
hint: It's what a rubber ball does.
funFact: Larry D. Mann, who voices the prospector, originally voiced the snowman narrator too, before Burl Ives took over the role.

question: The elves proudly perform their new song for Santa. Finish his grumpy review: “Hmm. Well, it…”
hint: Not quite ready for the big show.
funFact: The song they'd rehearsed so hard is “We Are Santa's Elves.”

question: Rudolph and Hermey, two runaway outcasts, sing a duet together. What's the song called?
hint: They sing about being a pair of oddballs.
funFact: From 1965 it was swapped out for a song called “Fame and Fortune,” and the original wasn't restored until 1998.

question: The special's stop-motion puppet animation, nicknamed “Animagic,” was filmed in which country?
hint: Land of the Rising Sun.
funFact: Animator Tadahito Mochinaga supervised the puppet work at a studio in Tokyo.

question: After the 1964 premiere, viewers wrote in about a loose end. What scene was added in 1965 to fix it?
answer: Santa picking up the Misfit Toys
accept: Santa stopping at the Island of Misfit Toys
Santa going back for the Misfit Toys
hint: Think about a promise Rudolph made on his journey.
funFact: The original Rudolph and Santa puppets sold at auction in 2020 for $368,000.

question: What's the name of the young buck who befriends Rudolph at the Reindeer Games, until he sees Rudolph's glowing nose?
hint: His name is also a spicy cinnamon candy.
funFact: After the nose comes off, Coach Comet bans Rudolph from the Reindeer Games.

question: What kind of creature is King Moonracer, who rescues unloved toys?
hint: He's the king of the jungle, with an upgrade.
funFact: He gathers unloved toys from around the world and keeps them on his island until they find children who will love them.

movie: Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town (1970)
question: What is the name of the grumpy, toy-hating mayor of Sombertown?
hint: His name sounds like a mouthful of hamburgers.
funFact: Voice actor Paul Frees plays him, plus the Kringle brothers and a crowd of townspeople and soldiers.

movie: Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town (1970)
question: What kind of animal is Topper, the little friend Kris meets on his way to Sombertown?
hint: A flightless bird that always looks dressed for a formal dinner.
funFact: Kris later marries the schoolteacher Jessica, who becomes Mrs. Claus.

movie: Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town (1970)
question: What simple toy does Kris give the scary Winter Warlock, melting his icy heart?
hint: It runs on tracks.
funFact: Kris then helps him change his ways with the song “Put One Foot in Front of the Other.”

movie: Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town (1970)
question: Why does Sombertown's grumpy mayor ban all toys?
answer: He trips over a toy duck
accept: He slipped on a toy duck
hint: It all started with a painful fall.
funFact: Kris gets around the ban by sneaking down chimneys and leaving toys in the children's stockings.

movie: Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town (1970)
question: How do Kris's reindeer learn to fly?
answer: They eat the Winter Warlock's magic feed corn
hint: A magical snack from a reformed villain.
funFact: The flying reindeer help Kris and his friends escape from jail.

question: How much does Lucy charge at her “Psychiatric Help” booth?
hint: Less than a dime.
funFact: Lucy's advice booth first appeared in the Peanuts comic strip in 1959.

question: What does Snoopy decorate to win the neighborhood lights and display contest?
hint: It's where he sleeps, up on the roof.
funFact: Charlie Brown is dismayed that even his own dog has gone commercial.

question: The gang wants a big, shiny aluminum tree. What kind of tree does Charlie Brown bring back?
hint: It droops when he hangs a single ornament on it.
funFact: Lucy's actual order: “Get the biggest aluminum tree you can find, Charlie Brown, maybe painted pink.”

question: Finish Sally's letter to Santa: “Just send money. How about…”
hint: Two kinds of paper bills.
funFact: Sally also explains that all she wants is her fair share.

question: Which jazz pianist composed the music, including “Christmas Time Is Here”?
hint: His trio also recorded the bouncy “Linus and Lucy” theme.
funFact: Children from a church choir in San Rafael, California, sang “Christmas Time Is Here.”

question: Finish Lucy's complaint: “Christmas is a big commercial racket. It's run by a big…”
hint: A shadowy organization from back East.
funFact: The child actors found phrases like “Eastern syndicate” hard to pronounce, and Sally's voice actress was too young to read, so she was fed her lines one at a time.

question: Charles Schulz flatly refused to add something almost every TV cartoon comedy had in 1965. What was it?
hint: Audience reactions that weren't really live.
funFact: CBS executives also disliked its slow pace, yet it drew about 45% of the TV audience on premiere night.

question: Finish the lyric: “You're as cuddly as a cactus, you're as charming as an…”
hint: A slippery, snake-like fish.
funFact: Dr. Seuss wrote the lyrics himself, and Albert Hague composed the music.

question: At the Whos' feast at the end, what does the Grinch himself carve?
hint: Its name rhymes with “feast.”
funFact: Cindy Lou Who gives Max the very first slice.

question: Little Cindy Lou Who catches the Grinch stuffing her family's tree up the chimney. What does he say he's doing with it?
answer: Taking it to his workshop to fix a light that won't light on one side
accept: A light won't light on one side
Taking it to his workshop to fix it
hint: He claims it's just a repair job.
funFact: Boris Karloff, famous as Frankenstein's monster, voices both the Grinch and the narrator.

question: Which legendary Looney Tunes animator, a co-creator of Wile E. Coyote and the Road Runner, directed the 1966 special?
hint: His first name rhymes with “duck.”
funFact: He and Dr. Seuss had teamed up years earlier on the World War II Army cartoons starring Private Snafu.

question: Who plays the Grinch in Ron Howard's 2000 live-action movie?
hint: He also starred in The Mask and Ace Ventura.
funFact: His makeup took up to two and a half hours a day, so producers hired a former Navy SEAL to teach him how to endure torture.

question: Finish the Grinch's schedule: “4:00, wallow in self-pity. 4:30, stare into the abyss. 5:00, solve world hunger…”
hint: He wants zero credit for it.
funFact: Anthony Hopkins narrates the film, and he recorded all of his narration in a single day.

question: Which Sherlock and Doctor Strange star voices the Grinch in Illumination's 2018 movie?
hint: His first name is also a famous eggs dish.
funFact: Pharrell Williams narrates the 2018 film.

question: What does the Pumpkin King mistakenly call Santa Claus?
hint: Sounds like a beach plus a lobster's pincers.
funFact: He asks Sally, the rag doll who secretly loves him, to make his Santa suit.

question: Finish the opening line of the song “What's This?”: “What's this? What's this? There's color…”
hint: All over the place.
funFact: The film earned an Oscar nomination for Best Visual Effects, a first for an animated film.

question: Lock, Shock and Barrel deliver the kidnapped Santa to which bug-filled, burlap-sack villain?
hint: He sings a jazzy number while rolling dice.
funFact: He's voiced by Ken Page, who originated Old Deuteronomy in Cats on Broadway.

question: Sally tries to ground the Pumpkin King's Christmas Eve sleigh ride by pouring out a magic potion. What weather does it create?
hint: It's the weather that made Santa need Rudolph in the famous song.
funFact: It nearly works, until Zero's glowing nose lights the way and he's sent “to the head of the team.”

question: Dr. Finkelstein grumbles that Sally has twice this month slipped which poison into his tea so she could run off?
hint: A poisonous plant whose name sounds like an evening shadow.
funFact: Later she spikes his soup, but he grumbles, “Nothing's more suspicious than frog's breath,” and won't swallow a spoonful until she tastes it.

question: What does the boy choose as the first gift of Christmas?
accept: A bell from a reindeer's harness
hint: It rings, but grown-ups can't hear it.
funFact: By the end, even his sister Sarah can no longer hear it ring.

question: During the big musical number on the train, what drink do the dancing waiters serve?
hint: It's served steaming in mugs.
funFact: The song shares the drink's name: “Hot Chocolate.”

question: What word does the conductor punch into the boy's ticket at the end?
hint: It's the theme of the whole movie.
funFact: The girl's ticket says LEAD, and the know-it-all's says LEARN.

question: Who is the ghostly figure who helps the boy across the roof of the moving train?
hint: A wandering vagabond who rides the rails.
funFact: A deleted scene on the home release reveals he's the ghost of a hobo who once rode on the train's roof.

question: Guinness World Records calls this the first film made entirely with which moviemaking technique?
hint: Actors wore suits dotted with tiny markers so computers could record their every move.
funFact: Its budget, about $165 million, was the highest ever for an animated feature at the time.

question: Who plays George Bailey?
hint: He also starred in Vertigo and Mr. Smith Goes to Washington.
funFact: It was his first film after serving as a bomber pilot in World War II.

question: Finish George's offer to Mary: “You want the moon? Just say the word, and I'll throw a…”
answer: Lasso around it and pull it down
hint: A cowboy's rope trick.
funFact: On that same walk home they throw rocks at the old Granville house to make wishes, and it later becomes their home.

question: When George gets his life back, what does he find in his pocket?
hint: Something his little daughter had asked him to fix.
funFact: His crisis began when Uncle Billy misplaced $8,000 of the Building and Loan's money.

question: At the high school dance, George and Mary dance until the gym floor opens up. What do they fall into?
hint: Bring your swimsuit.
funFact: The pool is real. It's under the gym floor at Beverly Hills High School.

question: In the world where George was never born, what is his hometown called?
hint: It's named after the town's greedy banker.
funFact: The film's snow was a new mix of foamite, soap flakes, water and sugar. Before that, movie snow was often made of cornflakes.

question: George's pals Bert and Ernie share names with two Muppets. Bert is a cop. What does Ernie do for a living?
hint: You'd hail him on the street.
funFact: Sesame Street writer Jerry Juhl confirmed that, according to producer Jon Stone, the shared names were just a coincidence.

question: Clarence, Angel Second Class, carries a copy of which Mark Twain book?
hint: Its hero tricks his friends into whitewashing a fence.
funFact: He leaves it for George inscribed: “Remember, no man is a failure who has friends.”

question: Kris tells a Macy's shopper, “Our skates are very good, but not quite good enough.” Which rival store does he send her to?
hint: A famous New York store whose name starts with G.
funFact: He also sends a mother to Schoenfeld's on Lexington Avenue for an $8.50 fire engine.

question: What does little Susan ask Kris to get her for Christmas?
hint: She tore its picture out of a magazine.
funFact: In the final scene, Fred and Doris find a cane just like Kris's inside that very house.

question: How does lawyer Fred Gailey finally prove in court that Kris is Santa Claus?
answer: The Post Office delivers Santa's letters to Kris
accept: Mail to Santa delivered to him
hint: A federal agency gets involved.
funFact: The studio released this Christmas classic in June 1947, believing more people go to the movies in warm weather.

question: In the 1994 remake, what does Susan hand the judge that wins the case?
answer: A Christmas card with a dollar bill
accept: A dollar bill with “In God We Trust” circled
hint: George Washington's face is involved.
funFact: She circled “In God We Trust”: if the government can trust without proof, so can New York.

question: Macy's wouldn't take part in the 1994 remake. What's the name of the fictional store that hires Kris instead?
hint: Sounds like what a naughty child finds in their stocking.
funFact: Richard Attenborough, Jurassic Park's John Hammond, plays Kris.

question: In Home Alone, finish the gangster's line from the old movie Kevin watches: “Keep the change…”
hint: He's insulting the person he's talking to.
funFact: Kevin plays the scene on his VCR to scare off the Little Nero's pizza delivery guy.

question: In Home Alone, what kind of creepy pet does Kevin's big brother Buzz keep in his room?
hint: It has eight hairy legs.
funFact: Yes, that's a real, live tarantula Kevin plops onto Marv's face.

question: In Home Alone's most famous scene, Kevin slaps something on his cheeks and screams. What is it?
hint: It's a grooming product from his dad's bathroom.
funFact: Macaulay Culkin was told to pull his hands away before screaming, but he kept them on his cheeks, and that take became iconic.

question: In Home Alone, which actress plays Kevin's mom, Kate, who famously screams “KEVIN!” on the plane?
hint: She later played Moira Rose on Schitt's Creek.
funFact: Catherine O'Hara also voiced Sally, the rag doll, in The Nightmare Before Christmas.

question: What's the title of the black-and-white gangster movie Kevin watches in Home Alone?
hint: The first word is a kind of heavenly being.
funFact: It isn't a real old movie: it was shot just for Home Alone, as a nod to the 1938 James Cagney film Angels with Dirty Faces.

question: In Home Alone, Buzz tells Kevin a spooky rumor about their neighbor Old Man Marley. What nickname does Buzz give him?
hint: It includes the name of a city in Indiana.
funFact: Marley turns out to be a kind, lonely old man who rescues Kevin from the burglars.

question: In Home Alone, Kate hitches a ride home with Gus Polinski, the “Polka King of the Midwest.” What's his band called?
hint: It's named after a city in Wisconsin.
funFact: John Candy shot all his scenes in about one day and improvised much of his dialogue.

question: Which composer earned two Oscar nominations for Home Alone's music?
hint: He also scored Star Wars, Jaws and the first Harry Potter films.
funFact: One nomination was for the carol “Somewhere in My Memory,” with lyrics by Leslie Bricusse.

movie: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992)
question: In Home Alone 2, Kevin ends up in New York. Where is the rest of the McCallister family spending Christmas?
hint: Think sunshine, palm trees and beaches.
funFact: This time Kevin isn't left at home: he boards the wrong plane at the airport.

movie: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992)
question: In Home Alone 2, which famous New York hotel does Kevin check into using his dad's credit card?
hint: It overlooks Central Park on Fifth Avenue.
funFact: The Plaza's suspicious concierge is played by Tim Curry, the frantic butler from the comedy Clue.

movie: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992)
question: In Home Alone 2, what's the name of the handheld tape recorder Kevin uses to disguise his voice and prank people?
hint: Kevin uses its slow-down feature to sound like a grown-up.
funFact: Tiger Electronics built it as a movie prop, and the real toy became a must-have for Christmas 1993.

movie: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992)
question: In Home Alone 2, what's the name of the toy store that Harry and Marv plan to rob on Christmas Eve?
hint: It's named after its kind, elderly owner.
funFact: Its kind owner, Mr. Duncan, was donating the store's Christmas proceeds to a children's hospital.

movie: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992)
question: In Home Alone 2, what gift does Kevin give the Pigeon Lady in Central Park as a sign of friendship?
hint: It's a bird ornament from the toy store's Christmas tree.
funFact: The Pigeon Lady is played by Brenda Fricker, an Oscar winner for My Left Foot.

question: In Elf, finish Buddy's advice to Jovie: “The best way to spread Christmas cheer is…”
answer: Singing loud for all to hear
accept: Singing loudly for all to hear
hint: It rhymes with “cheer.”
funFact: At the end, Jovie leads a crowd singing “Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town” to power Santa's sleigh.

question: In Elf, Buddy bursts into a little New York diner to congratulate them on having the world's best… what?
hint: It's a hot drink.
funFact: Peter Billingsley, Ralphie from A Christmas Story, pops up in Elf as Ming Ming, an elf at the North Pole.

question: In Elf, a snowball smacks Buddy in the face. Finish his yelp: “Ow! Son of a…”
hint: It's a wooden Christmas figure with a big jaw.
funFact: Buddy then single-handedly wins the snowball fight for his half brother, Michael.

question: In Elf, which Christmas-season duet does Buddy hear Jovie singing in the store's locker-room shower?
hint: It's a flirty duet about a guest who wants to leave on a snowy night.
funFact: Zooey Deschanel, who plays Jovie, is a real singer and later formed the duo She & Him.

question: In Elf, which Godfather actor plays Buddy's workaholic dad, Walter Hobbs?
hint: In The Godfather, he played hot-headed Sonny Corleone.
funFact: At the start of the film, Walter is on Santa's naughty list.

question: In Elf, Buddy mistakes the grumpy children's author Miles Finch for an elf. Which actor plays him?
hint: He later won Emmys as Tyrion Lannister on Game of Thrones.
funFact: Miles warns, “Call me elf one more time!” Buddy's very next line: “He's an angry elf.”

question: In Elf, during his all-night makeover of the store's Santaland, Buddy recreates what famous painting on an Etch A Sketch?
hint: It hangs in the Louvre in Paris.
funFact: At the North Pole, Buddy's job was building Etch A Sketches, and he finished only 85 in a day, way short of his quota.

question: Elf's director also plays the Hobbs family's doctor, who confirms Buddy is Walter's son. Who is he?
hint: He went on to direct Iron Man.
funFact: He also voiced the arctic puffin and Mr. Narwhal, uncredited.

question: In Christmas Vacation, the Griswolds find the perfect tree out in the country. What has Clark forgotten to bring?
accept: Something to cut it down with
hint: It's a tool with a jagged blade.
funFact: The film skips the digging: next thing you see, the tree is strapped to the car, roots and all.

question: In Christmas Vacation, what animal leaps out of the Griswolds' Christmas tree and causes chaos?
hint: It's a bushy-tailed critter that loves acorns.
funFact: Christmas Vacation was written by John Hughes, who wrote Home Alone a year later.

question: In Christmas Vacation, Aunt Bethany is asked to say grace. What does she recite instead?
hint: Schoolkids say it facing the flag.
funFact: Aunt Bethany was played by Mae Questel, the longtime voice of Betty Boop and Olive Oyl.

question: In Christmas Vacation, what's the name of Cousin Eddie's big dog?
hint: It's a gross word for what comes out of your nose.
funFact: Eddie promises Clark that if he gives Snots a belly rub, the dog will “love you till the day you die.”

question: In Christmas Vacation, what are the first names of the Griswolds' snooty yuppie neighbors?
hint: The wife is played by Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Elaine on Seinfeld.
funFact: Their last name is Chester.

question: In Christmas Vacation, which relative says at the dinner table, “Save the neck for me, Clark”?
hint: He shows up uninvited in a rusty RV.
funFact: Randy Quaid first played Cousin Eddie in National Lampoon's Vacation (1983).

question: In Christmas Vacation, which future Big Bang Theory star plays Clark's son, Rusty?
hint: On The Big Bang Theory, he played Leonard.
funFact: Juliette Lewis plays Rusty's sister, Audrey.

question: Before his wild sled ride in Christmas Vacation, Clark coats the sled with an experimental product his company is working on. What is it?
hint: It's meant for pans, not sleds.
funFact: Clark is going for a new “amateur recreational saucer-sled land-speed record.”

question: In A Christmas Story, Flick takes a dare at school. What does he get stuck to the frozen flagpole?
hint: Open your mouth and stick it out.
funFact: The real flagpole was sheathed in plastic, and a hidden suction device held Scott Schwartz's tongue to it, so nothing actually froze.

question: In A Christmas Story, the Old Man reads FRAGILE on a crate as “Fra-gee-lay.” What does he decide it must be?
hint: Think pizza, pasta and Rome.
funFact: Inside the crate is the infamous leg lamp, the Old Man's “major award.”

question: In A Christmas Story, what embarrassing gift does Aunt Clara send Ralphie?
hint: It has long floppy ears and a fluffy tail.
funFact: The Old Man says Ralphie looks like “a deranged Easter Bunny.”

question: In A Christmas Story, Ralphie finally decodes Little Orphan Annie's secret message. What does it say?
answer: Be sure to drink your Ovaltine
hint: It's a plug for the radio show's sponsor, a malted milk drink.
funFact: Ralphie's disgusted verdict: “A crummy commercial?!”

question: In A Christmas Story, after the Bumpus hounds devour the turkey, where do the Parkers eat Christmas dinner?
hint: They're served a whole roast duck.
funFact: Ralphie remembers it as the Christmas they were introduced to “Chinese turkey.”

question: In A Christmas Story, Schwartz breaks schoolyard etiquette when he dares Flick. Which step in the order of dares does he skip?
hint: Ralphie's narration says Schwartz went “right for the throat.”
funFact: Flick stays stuck to the pole until the fire department arrives to free him.

question: In A Christmas Story, what's the name of the yellow-eyed bully who torments Ralphie and his friends?
hint: His sidekick is Grover Dill.
funFact: The film is set in fictional Hohman, Indiana, based on Jean Shepherd's hometown of Hammond.

question: In Die Hard, McClane hides by crawling through what part of the building, joking, “Now I know what a TV dinner feels like”?
hint: It's a cramped metal tunnel behind the ceiling grilles.
funFact: Die Hard opened in theaters in July 1988, which fuels the yearly “is it a Christmas movie?” debate.

question: In Die Hard, which actor plays the suave villain Hans Gruber, in his first film role?
hint: He later played Professor Snape in the Harry Potter films.
funFact: McClane's wife, Holly, goes by her maiden name, Gennero, at work.

question: In Die Hard, a fellow plane passenger tells McClane to beat jet lag by taking off his shoes and socks and doing what?
accept: Walk barefoot and make fists with his toes
hint: It's done on the rug, with your feet.
funFact: Taking that advice is why McClane spends the whole adventure barefoot.

question: In Die Hard, Argyle the limo driver plays “Christmas in Hollis.” Which hip-hop group recorded it?
hint: They also had a hit with Aerosmith on “Walk This Way.”
funFact: When McClane grumbles, Argyle insists it is Christmas music.

question: In The Santa Clause, Scott Calvin startles Santa on Christmas Eve. What does Santa fall off of?
hint: It's where a sleigh would land.
funFact: Scott's hair turns white, and he grows a beard he can't shave off.

question: In The Santa Clause, after Scott burns the turkey, where do he and Charlie end up eating Christmas Eve dinner?
hint: It's a diner chain famous for its Grand Slam breakfast.
funFact: Scott's sales pitch to a skeptical Charlie: “Everybody likes Denny's. It's an American institution.”

question: In The Santa Clause, what's the name of the sarcastic head elf who tells Scott he's now Santa?
hint: He shares his name with a big rescue dog: the St. ___.
funFact: Bernard is played by David Krumholtz, later the star of TV's Numb3rs.

question: In The Santa Clause, finish the card Santa leaves behind: “If something should happen to me, put on my suit…”
answer: The reindeer will know what to do
accept: Reindeer will know what to do
hint: Santa's flying team will take it from there.
funFact: The fine print is the “Santa Clause”: whoever puts on the suit becomes the new Santa.

question: In The Santa Clause, Judy the elf's hot cocoa recipe is “Not too hot, extra chocolate…” and what else?
hint: It's how James Bond takes his martini.
funFact: Judy's boast: “My own recipe. Took me 1,200 years to get it right.”

question: In Jingle All the Way, a dad races around on Christmas Eve hunting for which sold-out action figure?
hint: He's a TV superhero with a jetpack.
funFact: The hero's catchphrase is “It's Turbo time!”

question: Which action-movie star plays Howard Langston, the toy-hunting dad in Jingle All the Way?
hint: He played the Terminator.
funFact: Howard's son, Jamie, is played by Jake Lloyd, later young Anakin Skywalker in Star Wars: Episode I.

question: In Jingle All the Way, which comedian plays Myron, the frazzled mailman chasing the same toy?
hint: He's a one-name stand-up comic who shares his name with a legendary sailor.
funFact: Myron later dresses as the superhero's archenemy, Dementor, at the big parade.

question: In Jingle All the Way, what's the name of Turbo-Man's sidekick?
hint: It's also the word for the extra rocket that gives a spacecraft its push at liftoff.
funFact: Curtis Armstrong, Booger from Revenge of the Nerds, has a cameo as a chain-smoking Booster performer at the parade.

question: Which Ghostbusters star plays the cold-hearted TV boss Frank Cross in Scrooged?
hint: He also starred in Groundhog Day.
funFact: His real-life brothers Brian Doyle-Murray, John Murray and Joel Murray all appear in the film.

question: In Scrooged, what does the Ghost of Christmas Past drive?
hint: It's yellow and has a meter.
funFact: The cab-driving ghost is played by David Johansen, singer of the New York Dolls.

question: In Scrooged, the sweet-looking Ghost of Christmas Present bashes Frank with which kitchen appliance?
hint: It makes your breakfast bread crispy.
funFact: Bill Murray insisted Carol Kane hit him for real, and in one scene she yanked his lip so hard it tore.

question: In Scrooged, which Olympic gymnast plays Tiny Tim in Frank's live TV version of A Christmas Carol?
hint: She won all-around gold at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics.
funFact: Frank's network, IBC, also casts comedian Buddy Hackett as Scrooge.

question: In Christmas with the Kranks, Luther and Nora plan to sit out the holidays and take what kind of trip instead?
hint: They'd be sailing to sunny islands.
funFact: Tim Allen and Jamie Lee Curtis play Luther and Nora Krank.

question: Christmas with the Kranks is based on which John Grisham novel?
hint: The title is exactly what the Kranks plan to do.
funFact: The screenplay was written by Chris Columbus, director of the first two Home Alone movies.

question: In Christmas with the Kranks, the couple won't put their giant snowman up on the roof. What two-word protest do the neighborhood kids chant?
hint: It names the famous snowman from the song.
funFact: Their daughter Blair's surprise visit home from Peru sends the Kranks scrambling to throw Christmas together after all.

question: In Jack Frost (1998), Michael Keaton plays a musician dad who comes back to life as what?
hint: He needs cold weather to survive.

question: In Jack Frost (1998), what magic musical instrument helps bring Jack back to his son, Charlie?
